Benedykivtsi Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Benedykivtsi, Ukraine

Not demolished. Presumably established in the 19th century and depicted on an 1865 cadastral map, this cemetery's latest documented tombstone was initially recorded at 1907 though a further preserved gravestone dates to 1940, suggesting continued use until WWII. Jews are believed to have arrived in the mid-18th century; population reached 177 by 1880 (of 526 total residents), declining to 163 by 1921 (Czechoslovak period). A Jewish-owned alcohol factory operated in the village; population reached 161 by 1930. Hungarian forces arrived March 1939, persecuting Jews and forcing them from their occupations; population reached 188 by 1941, when area Jews were drafted into forced labor battalions, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. Some families without Hungarian citizenship were expelled to Kamianets-Podilskyi and murdered; the remaining 150 Benedykivtsi Jews were deported to Auschwitz in mid-May 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
